title: docs: the worker.reference.md LANDING rule still says "use no git command"; align it with task-b5c8fd34's resume prompt (read-only git allowlist, merged-tree verification)
description:
Follow-up to task-b5c8fd341d4f48f89f5056b176622428. That task rewrites the LANDING-CONFLICT/LANDING-RETRY resume prompt in scripts/moe-agent.{sh,ps1}. It drops "no git commands" and appends one identical rule (sh `resume_rule`, ps1 `$resumeRule`) to both lines:
- HEAD can lack the merged target.
- A verification snapshot built from HEAD (`git archive HEAD`, or a clone checked out at HEAD) is built from the worktree's tracked files instead.
- Git stays read-only: only git status, git diff, git log, git show, git ls-files and git rev-parse may run. Every git write stays forbidden.

docs/roles/worker.reference.md :97 (the LANDING rule) still says "Edit files only: use no git command (commit, merge, reset, checkout, abort) ... Then re-run the plan's verification command". That now contradicts the prompt. A worker who reads the reference gets the same mixed signal that stalled WT-14's resume (msg-c9029b23).

This row only aligns the docs with the landed wrapper text: read the landed `resume_rule` line, never a planned copy. The doc is vendored, so packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts must be regenerated in a clone with history and applied with the Edit tool (Serena convention-role-doc-edits-regenerate-initfiles). worker.md's pointer "(edit files only; leave git to the wrapper)" still holds for git writes and may stay unchanged. The dated design record docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md stays out of scope.
definitionOfDone: docs/roles/worker.reference.md's LANDING rule no longer says "use no git command"; it names the same read-only allowlist as the landed resume rule (git status, git diff, git log, git show, git ls-files, git rev-parse), keeps every git write forbidden, and tells the worker to build a HEAD-based verification snapshot from the worktree's tracked files.

packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts is regenerated from the edited doc in a clone with history (marker sha and SHIPPED_ROLE_BODY_SHAS), and its diff touches only the worker.reference.md entry.

npm run lint passes, and packages/moe-daemon src/util/initFiles.test.ts, src/util/targetedContextGuidance.test.ts and src/util/qaCommitPolicy.test.ts pass in a Linux snapshot, with the exact commands and counts in the completion evidence.

implementationPlan.description:
Regenerate the daemon's vendored copy, and apply it with the Edit tool. Read mem:convention-role-doc-edits-regenerate-initfiles and mem:gotcha-daemon-linux-snapshot-gate.

1. Build a generator snapshot at the SAME base that checkRefs[2] and [3] use.
   - From the worktree root, compute B with their B=... expression. It is MERGE_HEAD under a pending merge. Otherwise it is the newest commit whose subject does not start with wip(task- or sync(task-.
   - Run S=$(mktemp -d), then git clone -q --shared --no-checkout . "$S/repo", then git -C "$S/repo" checkout -q --detach "$B".
   - Copy ONLY the edited docs/roles/worker.reference.md into $S/repo/docs/roles/.
   - In $S/repo/packages/moe-daemon, run the npm ci and generate-init-files part of checkRefs[3], under the same env -i and PATH.
   - Expect 'Generated ... (8 role docs + 3 subagents, sha-stamped)'.
   Why B and not HEAD: a worktree completion lands as ONE squashed commit, so a wip checkpoint holding a draft of the doc never reaches the target. A clone at HEAD would list that draft's body sha, and QA's re-run on the landed target would then fail the cmp. The prototype confirmed it: a HEAD base differs, while the B base matches.

2. diff -U0 the worktree's packages/moe-daemon/src/generated/initFiles.ts against the clone's. Expect exactly 3 hunks, all in the worker.reference.md entry:
   - the 'worker.reference.md' ROLE_DOCS marker line (line 594), where sha=27bec85d5275 becomes the new sha;
   - the LANDING bullet line (692);
   - one new sha, inserted in sorted position, in the 'worker.reference.md' SHIPPED_ROLE_BODY_SHAS line (750).
   Reference: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/ee85bfb1-plan/proto-initFiles.diff. The sha values follow the rule's bytes.

3. Apply the hunks with the Edit tool. Unique anchors in the template literal:
   - the step-1 (a) sentence, which contains no backtick;
   - 'Markers left behind': insert the same ' Both prompts end with this rule, verbatim: <rule>' text right after the escaped moe.complete_task sentence before it. The rule has no backtick, backslash or '${', so it is carried unescaped;
   - the marker sha;
   - the new sha, between its sorted neighbours.
   The Edit tool trims a trailing space in new_string, so end each one on a non-space character. Never cp, mv or redirect the generated file into the tree (GLOBAL rail 3).

4. cmp the worktree's file against the clone's output. They must be equal.

Error handling:
- A hunk outside the worker.reference.md entry means the base copy was stale. Stop and report_blocked, naming that doc and the commit that changed it. DoD 2 allows only this entry.
- If npm ci or the generator fails, rerun once. If it fails again, report_blocked with the error tail and blockedOnTaskIds [].
- Never run npm in the worktree's packages or in the shared checkout (GLOBAL rail 1).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Four alternatives were rejected.
- Paraphrasing the rule with backticks: the paraphrase can drift from the prompt, and the check degrades into a phrase list. Quoting the landed rule keeps the doc and both prompts identical, and grep -F tests it.
- Also editing worker.md's pointer: the pointer is still true for git writes, the task allows leaving it, and editing it would add a second initFiles.ts entry, which DoD 2 forbids.
- WT-18c's clone at HEAD: in worktree mode, a wip checkpoint's draft would add a body sha that the squashed landing never ships, so QA's re-run on the target would fail the cmp.
- A test pinning doc and wrapper rule together permanently: out of scope, since this row only aligns the docs. It is worth a follow-up if the rule changes again.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- The generator lists every historical body sha of each role doc. It reads git log -- docs/roles/<f> at the clone's HEAD and adds the working copy. A docs row therefore needs a clone with history, plus a base whose history matches what the target will hold.
- Worktree completions land as single-parent squash commits. The task branch additionally holds wip(task-...) checkpoints and sync(task-...) merges of its own landed commits. So the newest commit not matching ^(wip|sync)\(task- is the right generator base, or MERGE_HEAD during a pending merge. QA's re-run on the landed target resolves it to HEAD.
- The four checkRefs each stay at or under the contract's 1000-char limit and run standalone. Joined with &&, they are the evidence command.
planningNotes.risks:
1. b5c8fd34 may land a different rule after QA. Quote the landed one: checkRefs[0] reads it from HEAD, so a planned copy fails.
2. WT-18 (task-1b2e6fe3, WORKING) may regenerate initFiles.ts for worker.md. The worker.md and worker.reference.md SHIPPED lines are adjacent (749 and 750), so whichever row lands second may take the LANDING-CONFLICT route. Resolve it by keeping both entries; checkRefs[2] and [3] then base on MERGE_HEAD, which is the merged target.
3. Under a LANDING resume, the prompt's rule allows only six read-only git commands. checkRefs[3] needs a scratch git clone and checkout under mktemp; these never touch this worktree's index, HEAD, refs or MERGE_HEAD. If you read the allowlist as forbidding that clone, ask the governor once in chat before running it (precedent msg-c9029b23). Do not improvise another snapshot: the generator needs history.
4. If the base's initFiles.ts is stale, checkRefs[3] says so. Then report_blocked; do not fold in foreign hunks.
5. The Edit tool trims a trailing space in new_string.
6. No npm in the shared checkout or the worktree's packages.
